display_name: Tamdhu 18 Year Old (Oloroso Sherry Cask Matured)
cask: Exclusively oloroso sherry-seasoned casks — combination of European and American oak, sourced from Jerez, Spain
outturn_or_availability: Limited release / core range (annual). Exact outturn N/A — not found

tasting.nose: Dry nutty sherry, cherry and plum, milk chocolate, rum raisin, citrus and baked/honeyed oats; orange zest and hazelnut milk chocolate (per retailer notes).
tasting.palate: Rich, complex and decadently sherried — vanilla, brown sugar, red apple and dried fruits, deep nutty richness, dark chocolate and toasted almonds, with a characteristic dryness.
tasting.finish: N/A — not found (no critic finish text exposed in the captured excerpts).
tasting.narrative: NOSE: dry, nutty oloroso — cherry and plum, milk chocolate and rum raisin, lifted by citrus and baked/honeyed oats; the retailer adds orange zest and hazelnut milk chocolate (Whiskey Wash, TWE). PALATE: rich and decadently sherried — vanilla, brown sugar, red apple and dried fruit over deep nutty richness, dark chocolate and toasted almonds, all carried on a characteristic dryness (Whiskey Wash). FINISH: not captured. This is Tamdhu's full-throttle oloroso statement at 46.8%, natural colour and un-chill-filtered, matured exclusively in European/American-oak sherry casks from Jerez. Whiskey Wash calls it 'a sherry bomb whisky at the height of its greatness'; it took a Double Gold at the San Francisco World Spirits Competition. VERDICT: a benchmark dry-sherried Speysider and a credible value play against Macallan at ~$200 — buy to drink. But be honest about the evidence: every datum here is a WebSearch snippet (WebFetch was 403 all run), no numeric expert score is confirmed, the finish is missing, and the only auction reads are stale 2024 figures. Coverage is thin; treat the score as provisional pending verbatim verification.
